Definition: from the base of G4213 with enclitic adverb of origin; from which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause:--whence.
BiblicalUsage: Pothen asks whence, from what place or source. Nathanael asks Jesus, whence knowest thou me, and James asks the churches, from whence come wars and fightings among you.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that whence questions expose the heart, because wars do not fall from the sky but rise from lusts within.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
